title: Integral affine generic-flat model with unchanged fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $r:Y_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$ be the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. There exists a nonempty affine open subscheme $W\subseteq Y_{\mathrm{red}}$ such that $W$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and, for $q:W\to Y$ the restriction of $r$, the pullback $g:X_W=X\times_Y W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite type, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The map $q$ is a homeomorphism onto a nonempty open subset $V_0\subseteq Y$ containing $\eta$. For every $w\in W$ the induced map $\kappa(q(w))\to\kappa(w)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and the canonical fibre comparison identifies $(X_W)_w$ with $X_{q(w)}$ over this field isomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. In particular the unique point $\eta_W$ above $\eta$ is generic in $W$, and the generic fibre of $g$ is locally of finite presentation over $\kappa(\eta_W)$.

proof.text: Put $S=Y_{\mathrm{red}}$. The reduction theorem makes $S$ reduced and $r:S\to Y$ a homeomorphism and a closed immersion. Let $\eta_S=r^{-1}(\eta)$. Since homeomorphisms preserve closures, $\overline{\{\eta_S\}}=S$, so $S$ is irreducible and nonempty. The reduced-and-irreducible characterization of integrality therefore makes $S$ integral.

source.place: Tag 0578, lemma-geometrically-reduced-generic-fibre, first proof paragraph; reduction Tag 054M and integral characterization Tag 01ON

proof.text: Form $h:X_S=X\times_Y S\to S$. Locally finite type and quasi-compactness are separately preserved by base change, so $h$ is finite type. Apply generic flatness with local finite presentation to $h$ over the integral scheme $S$. It gives a nonempty open $U\subseteq S$ on which $h_U:X_S\times_S U\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, structure-sheaf case; lemma-base-change-finite-type and Tag 01K5 for finite type after base change

proof.text: The generic point $\eta_S$ belongs to $U$: otherwise its closure would be contained in the proper closed subset $S\setminus U$. Choose an affine open $W$ of $S$ with $\eta_S\in W\subseteq U$, using the affine-open basis. Its local rings are those of $S$, so they are reduced. Also $\overline{\{\eta_S\}}^{\,W}=W$; thus $W$ is nonempty and irreducible, hence integral. Write $\eta_W$ for $\eta_S$ viewed in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0578, first proof paragraph, affine restriction and shrinking; Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; Properties Tag 01ON

proof.text: Let $q:W\hookrightarrow S\xrightarrow{r}Y$. The pullback $g:X_W=X\times_Y W\to W$ is finite type by the locally-finite-type and quasi-compact base-change assertions applied to $f$. By the universal property of fibre products, $X_W$ is canonically $(X_S\times_S U)\times_U W$, with the same projection to $W$. Consequently the flat base-change theorem and clause (3) of the finite-presentation permanence statement give flatness and local finite presentation of $g$.

source.place: Tag 0578 preparation as used in more-morphisms.tex; Tags 01U9 (lemma-base-change-flat) and 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Because $r$ is a homeomorphism, $V_0=r(W)$ is open in $Y$ and $q$ is a homeomorphism from $W$ onto $V_0$. It contains $\eta=q(\eta_W)$; injectivity gives the asserted uniqueness above $\eta$, and step 3 already proves genericity. For $w\in W$, the map $\kappa(r(w))\to\kappa(w\text{ in }S)$ is an isomorphism because $r$ is a closed immersion. The open inclusion $W\hookrightarrow S$ also induces a residue-field isomorphism. Their composite is exactly $\kappa(q(w))\to\kappa(w)$: on local rings the map for the composite is the composite, and passing to the quotients by maximal ideals gives the residue maps.

source.place: Tag 0578, first proof paragraph, bijection on points and unchanged fibres; schemes.tex Tag 01HH (open immersions) and morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (closed immersions)

proof.text: Apply the fibre-of-base-change statement to $f$ and $q$ at $w$. It identifies $(X_W)_w$ canonically with $X_{q(w)}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q(w))}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$. By step 5 the field map is an isomorphism, so this is precisely the claimed identification over that field isomorphism. Finally the generic fibre morphism $g_{\eta_W}$ is the base change of the locally finitely presented morphism $g$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta_W)\to W$; clause (3) of the permanence statement makes it locally of finite presentation.
